title: Late signalling interface change
problem: Approve a late signalling interface change before system integration after a standards clarification.
context: Integration had started, access windows were fixed and three suppliers shared the affected interface.
decision: Approve conditionally with a 10-day design freeze, named interface owner and protected regression-test window.
outcome: Change delivered. Eight days of delay against a 24-day exposure; no safety retest repeated.

title: Passenger information requirement added
problem: Late passenger-information functionality requested during systems integration.
context: Software release was six weeks from test entry and requirements ownership was split across client teams.
decision: Defer non-regulatory functions and approve the minimum compliant change behind a feature flag.
outcome: Core requirement entered service on time. Deferred functions followed 31 days later.

title: Second shift before access release
problem: Add a second installation shift to recover delay while workfront access remained constrained.
context: Only two of five work areas were available and specialist supervision could not cover both shifts.
decision: Approve the additional shift immediately without an access-readiness gate.
outcome: Cost increased but only one day was recovered. Crews waited 27% of paid hours.

title: Flood-wall foundation redesign
problem: Ground conditions required a foundation redesign after piling had mobilised.
context: Temporary works and marine permits constrained the remaining build sequence.
decision: Pause one workfront, prototype the revised detail and resequence unaffected wall sections.
outcome: Twenty-four days of forecast exposure avoided; prototype prevented repeat rework.

title: Firmware change during assurance
problem: Safety-related firmware defect identified during dynamic testing required an urgent change.
context: The test train and independent assessor had limited availability.
decision: Create a quarantined branch, replay the full evidence pack and keep the original release as rollback.
outcome: Assurance accepted first submission. Six-day delay with no later regression.

title: Clinical layout revision
problem: Clinical users requested a major layout revision after design approval.
context: Equipment orders were not placed, but statutory submission was due in three weeks.
decision: Run a five-day decision room, freeze adjacencies and submit unaffected zones separately.
outcome: Statutory date held for three zones. Revised clinical zone followed five days late.

title: Pump supplier substitution
problem: Replace a failing pump supplier without invalidating hydraulic design and approvals.
context: Long-lead manufacture drove commissioning and the alternate unit had different controls.
decision: Approve alternate supplier after a paid interface study and early factory witness test.
outcome: Commissioning began four days earlier than the revised plan. Interface issue found at factory.

title: Additional security screening route
problem: Security stakeholder added a screening route after interface configuration had begun.
context: Operational cutover could not move and simulation capacity was limited.
decision: Approve the full change and compress integrated testing to protect cutover.
outcome: Cutover moved 17 days after two integration defects escaped compressed testing.

title: Protection standard update
problem: New protection standard affected nine similar substations at different design maturity.
context: Applying one response to all sites would create unnecessary redesign on advanced sites.
decision: Segment sites by maturity and use three approved response patterns with a common evidence pack.
outcome: Seven sites absorbed the change within float; two advanced sites moved four days.

title: Maintenance access enhancement
problem: Operator requested additional maintenance access after structural steel fabrication.
context: The request improved whole-life operations but affected fabricated members and fire strategy.
decision: Reject physical change for day one and fund a removable access solution for the first maintenance cycle.
outcome: Entry into service held. Permanent enhancement installed during planned possession.

title: Identity provider replacement
problem: Replace the identity provider after privacy review during delivery.
context: Four services depended on authentication and user migration had not started.
decision: Build an adapter layer, dual-run providers and migrate one low-risk service first.
outcome: Seven-day delay. No service outage and adapter reused on two later programmes.

title: Facade material substitution
problem: Approve a facade material substitution after supplier insolvency.
context: Sample approval, fire evidence and procurement lead time all affected enclosure dates.
decision: Approve only after full-scale mock-up and independent evidence review; resequence internal zones.
outcome: Nine-day completion movement. Mock-up identified fixing change before bulk manufacture.

title: Parallel fit-out workfronts
problem: Open two additional fit-out workfronts to recover a station handover delay.
context: Design was stable and access, supervisors and materials were confirmed before approval.
decision: Approve staged acceleration after workfront-readiness checks and weekly productivity gates.
outcome: Nine days recovered. Productivity stayed within 6% of the original workfront.

title: Cooling controls modification
problem: Controls modification required after integrated thermal test failure.
context: Client migration date was fixed and repeat full-load test required specialist equipment.
decision: Approve modification with an independent test script review and a witnessed partial-load rehearsal.
outcome: Full-load retest passed first time. Migration proceeded four days later than baseline.

title: Cable route revision
problem: Environmental constraint required a cable route revision before contract award.
context: Survey data was incomplete but delaying award would lose the marine installation slot.
decision: Award a bounded early-works package and hold final route scope until targeted surveys completed.
outcome: Installation slot protected. Final route added two days and avoided a larger compensation event.

title: Archive environmental controls
problem: Archive humidity requirements were clarified after developed design.
context: Plant space and electrical capacity were already allocated.
decision: Approve enhanced controls after validating archive zones and removing blanket treatment elsewhere.
outcome: Net plant load reduced. Design moved one day and capital cost stayed within contingency.

title: CAB radio software freeze break
problem: Approve a late CAB radio software change during systems integration after a manufacturer notice.
context: Regression windows were booked and two other interfaces shared the same possession.
decision: Approve behind a named regression owner, freeze unrelated interface changes, and keep a rollback build.
outcome: Five-day delay; rollback unused and no repeated safety retest.

title: Additional CCTV coverage late
problem: Security added CCTV coverage after temporary works design was frozen.
context: Cable routes clashed with temporary works and the marine window was fixed.
decision: Defer permanent CCTV to the first maintenance window and approve a temporary coverage plan for day one.
outcome: Marine window held; permanent CCTV installed later without reopening temporary works.

title: Traction power trip threshold
problem: Change traction power trip thresholds after dynamic test trips delayed the test train plan.
context: Assessor availability was limited and the original settings were in the safety case.
decision: Quarantine the change, update the safety evidence pack, and replay only the affected test series.
outcome: Four-day slip; assessor accepted first resubmission.

title: Cable joint bay relocation
problem: Relocate a cable joint bay after unexpected utilities were found.
context: Outage slots were booked and civil crews were already on site.
decision: Pause the bay, prototype the relocated detail on a non-critical span, then release the outage sequence.
outcome: Seven days lost versus a 25-day exposure; prototype avoided a second redesign.

title: Sorter PLC firmware patch
problem: Apply a PLC firmware patch after an integration defect threatened cutover.
context: Cutover could not move and overnight test windows were scarce.
decision: Patch in a quarantined lane, keep full regression on the critical path, refuse a test waiver.
outcome: Two-day movement; no escaped defect at cutover.

title: Night works without access proof
problem: Start night works to recover delay before access and neighbour consents were confirmed.
context: Only one workfront was free and consents lagged the programme narrative.
decision: Refuse night works until consents and access were evidenced; approve daytime overtime instead.
outcome: Three days slipped; avoided a stop-notice that would have cost more.

title: Fire alarm cause-and-effect rewrite
problem: Late fire strategy rewrite required cause-and-effect changes during systems integration.
context: Commissioning was booked and soft landings with clinical users had started.
decision: Approve a time-boxed design freeze, protect the fire test window, and stage non-critical soft-landing tasks.
outcome: Six-day delay; fire tests passed without a second round.

title: Platform edge camera mandate
problem: A new platform-edge camera mandate arrived after detailed design freeze.
context: Cable capacity was tight and civils for mounting points affected possession plans.
decision: Segment stations by maturity; apply a common evidence pack and defer low-risk sites to the next possession cycle.
outcome: High-risk stations absorbed in float; deferred sites followed next cycle.

title: Status narrative denied a known finish slip
problem: Period progress report told the board the ready-for-service date was unchanged while the control schedule finish had moved by more than two months after late interface and procurement changes during systems integration.
context: Design freeze had slipped, long-lead procurement was re-sequenced, and the PMO covering note still said the programme was on track with no material change. Change authority was asked to note progress rather than decide.
decision: Reject the note-only path. Require a corrected narrative, named interface owner, protected regression window, and an explicit decision on whether ready-for-service remains contractual or must be re-baselined.
intervention: Correct narrative + conditional controls before approval
outcome: Board deferred approval for one cycle. Corrected pack admitted a 61-day movement; conditional controls limited further slip to 19 days versus a 70-day unmanaged exposure.
